instruction: List regular files above five hundred megabytes under workspace in descending byte size.
context: GNU find: -size +500M filters regular files larger than the threshold. -printf '%s %p\n' emits a leading byte count and pathname per newline-delimited record; sort -n can then compare that numeric field and -r reverses the order.

instruction: Show the twenty-five biggest regular files below /srv with byte counts.
context: GNU find -printf %s produces file size in bytes and %p the pathname. Putting size first gives sort -n a numeric key; -r orders largest first and head limits the already-ranked records.

instruction: Show the ten smallest files in downloads with their byte sizes.
context: find -printf '%s %p\n' creates numeric-size records. Plain sort -n keeps ascending numeric order, so head selects the smallest rather than the lexicographically earliest filenames.

instruction: List the twenty newest log files under logs with timestamps and paths.
context: GNU find -printf %T@ emits a sortable fractional modification timestamp before %p. Numeric reverse sort ranks newest first; printing only %p would give sort no timestamp field to compare.

instruction: Display the five oldest regular files beneath archive with modification timestamps.
context: find -printf %T@ supplies numeric modification time and %p supplies the associated path. Ascending sort -n places oldest timestamps first before head selects five records.

instruction: Emit all files under media as null-delimited size-and-path records sorted largest first.
context: GNU find -printf can terminate a complete size-and-path record with \0. sort -z consumes NUL-delimited records while -n compares the leading size and -r orders descending; -print0 alone would emit paths without a numeric field.

instruction: Sort asset file paths while retaining null delimiters for unusual filenames.
context: find -print0 emits NUL-delimited path records. GNU sort -z consumes and emits the same framing, so spaces and embedded newlines in filenames do not split records.

instruction: List ordinary documentation file paths alphabetically one per line.
context: find -print emits newline-delimited path records and plain sort consumes newline-delimited text lexicographically. This form is appropriate only when ordinary line-oriented pathname output is acceptable.

instruction: Run file on every item under uploads without breaking names containing whitespace.
context: find -print0 produces NUL-framed pathnames and xargs -0 consumes exactly that framing. -r avoids invoking file when find emits no records.

instruction: Emit null-delimited paths for regular cache files above two hundred megabytes without sorting them.
context: find -size +200M performs the size filter and -print0 emits only matched pathnames with NUL framing. No numeric consumer is requested, so a separate size column or sort stage would be unnecessary.

instruction: Rank files below reports by bytes using stat to produce the size field.
context: GNU stat -c '%s %n' prints byte size followed by filename for each path batched by find -exec {} +. The leading numeric field is what makes sort -n meaningful; -r places largest first.

instruction: Rank project directories from smallest to largest using human-readable sizes.
context: du -s emits one aggregate record per argument and -h formats its leading size with unit suffixes. sort -h understands those suffixes, unlike lexicographic sort or plain sort -n.
